issue: English calque: 'pergi' for a departing bus is unnatural — scheduled transport 'berangkat' (departs). Natives say 'Busnya baru saja berangkat', not 'bus ... pergi'.

fix.target: Bus ke bandara baru saja berangkat.
fix.english: The bus to the airport just left.

issue: Awkward mix of the ongoing-state marker 'masih' with a schedule phrase 'sampai malam' — natives say either 'masih buka' (still open now) or 'buka sampai malam' (open until night), not both stacked.

fix.english: That store is still open now.

issue: Calque of 'Where does this bus go?' — Indonesian destination questions for vehicles drop the verb: 'Bus ini ke mana?'. 'Bus ini pergi ke mana?' is textbook-English phrasing no native would use at a bus stop.

fix.grammar: Destination questions can drop the verb: Bus ini ke mana? (Where does this bus go?)

issue: 'mulai kerja baru itu' is an English calque of 'start that new job' — 'kerja' as a bare noun for 'a job' does not take 'baru itu' naturally; natives say 'mulai kerja di kantor baru' or 'mulai pekerjaan baru'.

fix.target: Kapan kamu mulai kerja di kantor baru?
fix.english: When do you start work at the new office?

issue: Stiff register: after the modal 'mau', conversational Indonesian uses the bare root ('mau beli'), which this deck itself models elsewhere (id-0191 'mau pesan', id-0210 'beli'). 'mau membeli' reads as written prose in a shopping context.

fix.target: Saya mau beli tiga kilo beras.
fix.english: I want to buy three kilos of rice.
fix.grammar: After mau, the bare root is natural in speech: mau beli = want to buy.

issue: Slightly unidiomatic: the set phrase is 'mandi air dingin' (take a cold shower); 'mandi dengan air dingin' is bookish instrumental phrasing.

fix.target: Setiap pagi saya mandi air dingin.
fix.english: Every morning I bathe with cold water.

issue: Wrong verb: 'mendengar' = to hear (perceive by chance); deliberate listening is 'mendengarkan'. The English gloss 'I listen to music' does not match 'mendengar musik' (I hear music). Classic dengar/dengarkan error.

fix.english: I listen to music while cooking.
fix.grammar: sambil = while (one person, two actions): makan sambil membaca = eat while reading.

issue: Register: 'kepada' is written/formal Indonesian; in neutral conversation people send messages 'ke' someone. Q2 card should model the conversational preposition.

fix.target: Saya mengirim pesan ke teman kerja.
fix.english: I send a message to a coworker.

issue: Missing benefactive -kan: reading a story aloud to someone is 'membacakan cerita'; 'membaca cerita untuk anaknya' is grammatical but not what natives say, and the card sits right after the -kan tip card (id-0180) without using the pattern.

fix.target: Dia membacakan cerita untuk anaknya setiap malam.
fix.english: She reads her child a story every night.
fix.grammar: -kan can mean doing it for someone: membaca (read) → membacakan (read aloud to someone).

issue: Register: 'pada akhir pekan' is written-style; conversational Indonesian drops 'pada' or uses 'di' for time expressions (the deck itself drops it in id-0148/id-0149).

fix.target: Kami membersihkan rumah di akhir pekan.
fix.english: We clean the house on the weekend.

issue: 'memulai pekerjaan' is report-speak (bureaucratese) for a daily-routine card; conversational Indonesian is 'mulai kerja / mulai bekerja' (compare the deck's own id-0139 'Saya mulai kerja jam delapan pagi').

fix.target: Saya mulai bekerja jam sembilan pagi.
fix.english: I start work at nine in the morning.

issue: Register: 'pada hari kerja' is stiff written style; conversation uses 'di hari kerja' or 'kalau hari kerja'.

fix.target: Kami tidur lebih awal di hari kerja.
